reason: While the text emphasizes Moses' leadership role as God's intermediary, it explicitly grants agency to the common people (עם). The people are commanded to sanctify themselves ('וְקִדַּשְׁתָּ֥ם'), wash their clothes ('וְכִבְּס֖וּ שִׂמְלֹתָֽם'), guard themselves from approaching the mountain ('הִשָּׁמְר֥וּ לָכֶ֛ם'), and refrain from sexual relations ('אַל־ תִּגְּשׁוּ אֶל־ אִשָּׁה'). These constitute active responsibilities and choices given to the general population, not merely passive reception of commands. The text depicts a hierarchical structure where Moses has closer access to God, but agency—the capacity to act and be responsible for one's actions—extends to the broader community as well.
